title: LLM-Derived Preference Judgments Are Not Self-Consistent
abstract: arXiv:2608.17644v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agents increasingly interpret a person's natural-language preferences by querying an LLM for numerical preference judgments, e.g., by asking how much the person would be willing to pay for an item. A growing body of work estimates a utility function from these judgments and then chooses actions based on their estimated utility. This pipeline assumes the judgments are approximately self-consistent: that a single utility function can reproduce them. But are they? To study this question, we measure the self-consistency of cardinal LLM preference judgments. For example, the difference in stated willingness-to-pay between two items should match the stated payment that makes a person indifferent to exchanging them. We develop statistical tests and interpretable measures of how far observed responses depart from the best-fitting self-consistent utility function. translated_title: 大语言模型衍生的偏好判断并非自洽
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17644v1 公告类型：新 摘要：智能体越来越多地通过查询大语言模型（LLM）来获取数值偏好判断，以解释个人的自然语言偏好，例如询问某人对某物品愿意支付多少金额。越来越多的研究从这些判断中估计效用函数，并根据估计的效用选择行动。这一流程假设判断大致是自洽的：即存在一个单一的效用函数可以重现它们。但事实真的如此吗？为研究此问题，我们测量了基数型LLM偏好判断的自洽性。例如，两个物品之间陈述的支付意愿差异，应等同于使个人在交换它们时无差异的陈述支付金额。我们开发了统计检验和可解释的度量方法，以评估观察到的响应偏离最拟合自洽效用函数的程度。在涵盖六个LLM的航班、公寓和酒店示例实验中，我们发现显著偏差。
tldr: 本文发现大语言模型生成的数值偏好判断（如支付意愿）在自洽性方面存在显著不足，即无法被单一效用函数一致重现，这挑战了基于LLM偏好估计的决策流程。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that numerical preference judgments (e.g., willingness-to-pay) derived from LLMs exhibit significant self-inconsistency, failing to be reproduced by a single utility function, which challenges LLM-based preference estimation pipelines.
